answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by grading the graders: every identity earns standing only when its peer grades match the eventual consensus. Like boats tied at a jetty, each agent's record is visible to all, and a velvet-smooth copy that grades its own clones soon drifts from the honest horizon of consensus. A sybil farm must therefore grade honestly, at full cost, on thousands of unrelated tasks to gain weight, while random or collusive grading steadily drains its standing to zero.
